newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to make paying bribes overseas a crime - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan to make paying bribes overseas a crime - paper.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto plans to submit a bill to parliament banning Japanese firms and individuals from offering bribes to foreign politicians and government officials, a major newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the government is to submit the bill, including penalties for bribery conducted abroad, to the autumn parliament session for implementation in 1998.
A government spokesman had no comment on the report.

The newspaper said illicit payments to foreign government officials had become an established practice among some Japanese firms to smooth foreign business operations, particularly when large-scale government-related projects were involved.
Japanese law has penal provisions for crimes committed overseas only in cases of murder, forgery and counterfeiting.

The newspaper said Japan also plans to join the United States in urging member nations of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) to ban illicit payments to foreign officials.

The United States, the only country which has laws banning international business bribery, has long urged other nations to abolish improper business practices such as bribery, as Washington says they hinder fair competition.
The Paris-based OECD, a forum for coordinating economic and social policies, agreed last year to criminalise foreign bribery in principle and ordered a study of how to do so.
